an9.63:0.3: Weaknesses in Training and Mindfulness Meditation
an9.63:1.1: “Bhikkhus, there are these five weaknesses when you’re training.
an9.63:1.3: Killing living creatures, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, and consuming beer, wine, and liquor intoxicants.
an9.63:1.4: These are the five weaknesses when you’re training.
an9.63:2.1: To give up these five weaknesses in your training you should develop the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.
an9.63:2.3: It’s when a bhikkhu meditates by observing an aspect of the body—ardently aware and comprehending, without craving and aversion towards the world
an9.63:2.4: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …
an9.63:2.5: They meditate observing an aspect of the mind …
an9.63:2.6: They meditate observing an aspect of principles—ardently aware and comprehending, without craving and aversion towards the world
an9.63:2.7: To give up those five weaknesses in your training you should develop these four kinds of mindfulness meditation.”
